title: Reviewer failures become named categories, and a run that could not run never approves
summary: This change makes a reviewer's failure legible without ever repeating the reviewer's own text. A new `failure` module classifies a failed or timed-out reviewer's stdout/stderr into a fixed category (credential, quota, model unavailable, schema rejected, unreachable, command line, permission, unknown), and `reviewers.rs` puts only that category, the exit code and the elapsed seconds into the reason. `osf review run` now writes its `--out` file before exiting non-zero when a reviewer tried and nothing answered, and the posted event follows the run's overall verdict: a run that could not run posts COMMENT instead of APPROVE. The CI workflow stops keeping and uploading reviewer homes, and a kept local home now has its seeded logins removed on every path out.

lanes.label: CI workflow
lanes.subtitle: GitHub Actions
lanes.summary: The reviewer jobs no longer set OSF_KEEP_REVIEW_HOME or TMPDIR, no longer create or upload a reviewer home, and still upload their saved answers after a red run.

lanes.label: osf CLI
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The command that runs a reviewer, saves its run, and decides the exit code and the posted event.

lanes.label: Reviewer runtime
lanes.subtitle: child process in a private home
lanes.summary: The spawned harness, its private home, and the pipes that carry its output back to osf.

lanes.label: Model providers
lanes.subtitle: external APIs
lanes.summary: The external services a reviewer talks to; their error text is what the classifier reads.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: reviewer jobs
nodes.summary: Each reviewer job runs `osf review run` in a container and uploads the saved answers. The change removes the reviewer-home directory, the OSF_KEEP_REVIEW_HOME and TMPDIR environment variables, and the 'Keep this reviewer's home' artifact step.

nodes.label: reviewer job
nodes.subtitle: codex / claude / opencode
nodes.summary: One matrix-style job per reviewer. It can now go red when the reviewer made attempts and none answered, and its upload steps run with `if: always()` so the saved answers still travel.

nodes.label: osf review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run_exit_code
nodes.summary: Runs one reviewer, saves its run to `--out`, and returns 0 when it answered, 2 when it tried and nothing answered, 2 on error. The file is written before the non-zero exit so the artifact explains the red job.

nodes.label: ReviewerRun
nodes.subtitle: never_answered()
nodes.summary: The saved record of one reviewer's lenses and attempts. `never_answered` is true when at least one lens had a context error or an attempt, and no attempt on any lens answered.

nodes.label: failure::classify
nodes.subtitle: Category
nodes.summary: Reads a reviewer's stdout and stderr and returns one fixed category. JSON fields such as statusCode, status, api_error_status, error.type and error.code are read first; plain-text patterns are the last resort. The category's phrase is osf's own wording, so it is safe to print.

nodes.label: run_child
nodes.subtitle: spawn, drain, classify
nodes.summary: Spawns the reviewer, drains both pipes, and on a non-zero exit or a timeout builds the reason from the exit code, the elapsed time and the classified category. The reviewer's own text is never put in the reason.

nodes.label: RunHome
nodes.subtitle: private home, retire()
nodes.summary: A private 0700 home for one reviewer run. It now remembers the seeded login paths and, when kept, removes them on every path out; if a login cannot be removed the whole home goes.

nodes.label: plan_review_for
nodes.subtitle: verdict to event
nodes.summary: Maps the run's overall verdict to the posted event: a blocking finding or a failed run requests changes, a could-not-run run posts COMMENT, a pass approves. `plan_review` keeps its findings-only behaviour for `osf review post`.

nodes.label: reducer::decide
nodes.subtitle: weighted_mean
nodes.summary: An empty lens set now yields CouldNotRun at every threshold, and `weighted_mean` returns None for it, so a review with no selected lens is never a pass.

nodes.label: answer::schema_for
nodes.subtitle: drops $schema and $id
nodes.summary: The schema handed to a harness no longer carries `$schema` or `$id`, which claude refuses to resolve; the file keeps them for editors. Validation reasons now hide reviewer-chosen property names behind `<field>`.

nodes.label: reviewer harness
nodes.subtitle: codex / claude / opencode
nodes.summary: The child process osf spawns. Its stdout and stderr are untrusted text that may hold a credential, so they are read for a category and never repeated.

nodes.label: stdout pipe
nodes.subtitle: drained by a thread
nodes.summary: Carries the reviewer's standard output back to osf, where it is parsed for the answer and, on failure, classified.

nodes.label: stderr pipe
nodes.subtitle: now read, never printed
nodes.summary: Previously drained and discarded. It is now joined and handed to the classifier, so a failure reason can name a category, but its text still never reaches osf's output, the journal, SARIF or a posted review.

nodes.label: provider API
nodes.subtitle: HTTP
nodes.summary: The model provider a reviewer calls. Its 401, 403, 429 and model-not-found responses are the shapes the classifier recognises.

edges.label: osf review run
edges.summary: The job invokes the CLI in a container. The change removes the home-keeping environment and the home artifact step.
The CLI runs the reviewer through run_child, which now classifies a failure instead of only naming the exit code.
The harness is spawned in its own process group with a private home.
The reviewer's answer and any error text arrive on standard output.
Standard error now carries the failure text into the classifier rather than being discarded.

edges.label: untrusted text in, category out
edges.summary: The classifier reads the reviewer's text and returns only a fixed category, so a credential in that text never reaches osf's output.
Standard output is read the same way, so the category does not depend on which stream held the text.
The category's phrase becomes the failure reason, alongside the exit code and elapsed seconds.
The home is created with the reviewer's login paths and retired on every path out, including spawn and wait failures.

edges.label: --out JSON
edges.summary: The run is saved before the exit code is decided, so a red job still leaves the file that explains it.
The run's lens verdicts feed the reducer, which now treats an empty set as could-not-run.

edges.label: overall verdict
edges.summary: The run's overall verdict now decides the posted event: could-not-run posts COMMENT, never APPROVE.

edges.label: APPROVE / COMMENT / REQUEST_CHANGES
edges.summary: The plan's event is what the last job posts, and the same verdict drives the CLI exit code.
The reviewer calls its provider; the provider's error responses are the shapes the classifier recognises.

edges.label: schema without $schema/$id
edges.summary: The answer schema handed to the harness no longer names the 2020-12 meta-schema, which claude refuses to resolve.

flows.title: A reviewer that tried and never answered
flows.summary: One reviewer job runs, the harness fails with a credential error, osf classifies the text into a category, saves the run, and exits non-zero so the job goes red while the artifact still explains why.

messages.label: exit 1, stderr: 401 Unauthorized
messages.note: The text may hold a credential, so it is never repeated.

messages.label: reviewer 'codex' exited with code 1 after 2.1 s: the provider rejected the credential
